original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-composition-gorenstein}
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms. Assume that the
fibres $X_y$, $Y_z$ and $X_z$ of $f$, $g$, and $g \circ f$ are
locally Noetherian.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ is Gorenstein
at $f(x)$, then $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$.
\item If $f$ and $g$ are Gorenstein, then $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein.
\item If $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $f$ is flat at $x$,
then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ is Gorenstein at $f(x)$.
\item If $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein and $f$ is flat, then
$f$ is Gorenstein and $g$ is Gorenstein at every point in
the image of $f$.
\end{enumerate}

final_content.statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be morphisms such that *all* fibres of $f,g,g\circ f$ are locally Noetherian. Then (1) if $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ at $f(x)$, $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$; (2) if $f$ and $g$ are Gorenstein everywhere, then $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein; (3) if $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $f$ is flat at $x$, then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ at $f(x)$; (4) if $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein everywhere and $f$ flat everywhere, then $f$ is Gorenstein everywhere and $g$ is Gorenstein **at points in the image of $f$**, not necessarily outside that image.
hypotheses: Three locally Noetherian fibre systems; additional flatness of f for converse directions.
conclusions: Four precise composition and descent implications for Gorenstein morphisms.

semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L6358 requires the fibres of f:X→Y, g:Y→Z and gf to be locally Noetherian, and gives FOUR implications. The proposal retains pointwise/local and global composition, the converses subject to f FLAT at x or globally, and correctly restricts the global conclusion for g to the IMAGE of f, not all Y.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-flat-Noetherian-gorenstein}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism
of $\textit{FTS}_S$. Let $x \in X$. If $f$ is flat, then
the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$,
\item $f^!\mathcal{O}_Y$ is isomorphic to an invertible object
in a neighbourhood of $x$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the set of points where $f$ is Gorenstein is
open in $X$.

final_content.statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and the category $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ of separated finite-type $S$-schemes. For $f:X\to Y$ therein, let $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ be the upper-shriek functor built from the right adjoint to proper pushforward on a compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\to Y$. In particular $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is a coherent bounded complex when $f$ is perfect. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ and $x\in X$. Then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ iff there exists an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ on which $f^!\mathcal O_Y|_U$ is **derived-invertible**, i.e. locally isomorphic to a shift of a line bundle. In particular the pointwise Gorenstein locus is open. This relative criterion uses the upper-shriek *complex*, not just its zeroth cohomology.
conclusions: Gorenstein at x iff f^!O_Y derived-invertible around x; locus open.

The final retains the flatness and local derived-invertibility rather than merely stalkwise rank one.
